answer: Hardware attestation can tie agent identities to scarce machines. Each key registers with a signed quote from a trusted enclave, and the forge contract counts keys per enclave: the k-th key on one chip locks 25×k² POA. One key locks 25, ten lock 9,625 in total, and 1,000 on one chip about 8.3 billion, far above the ~400k POA a whole epoch emits. Bonds return only after 30 active epochs, so a comet of keys that farms once and vanishes forfeits them. Cloned VMs replay one quote, which a mirror check of quote nonces catches. Weakness: renting many enclaves, though each is real hardware.
